result:
Round 32 is a **FAIL**. A built exactly what B specified, but the fix creates a new Medium bug in the normal edit flow.

**C-R32-01 (Medium, new):** after the user touches a fader, Delete stops working.
- **Steps:** real click on the music Volume fader, then a real click on the SFX clip (it becomes selected), then Delete or Backspace. Nothing happens: no deletion, no history entry, no status message.
- **Lane body:** the same happens after clicking an empty lane area.
- **Cause (code reading):** clicking a clip does not move focus off the fader, because the clip's pointerdown cancels the browser's default (`ArrangementClip.tsx:228`). The lane body cannot take focus either. The new guard then sees the fader still focused and ignores Delete.
- **Order matters:** B's order (click the clip, then focus the fader, then Delete) passes. The reverse order (fader first, then click a clip or lane) fails. This is a gap in B's spec, not a mistake by A.
- **Scope:** Volume, Master and Zoom deleted the clip in this sequence before round 32 and now do nothing. Pan already did nothing before round 32, because of A's round-31 workaround.
- **Coverage:** `fader-guards.test.tsx` sets focus directly, so it never sees this.
- **Evidence:** the repro is in `runs/dk-focus-retention.txt`. A run with focus on the page body is the control, and there Delete works.

Everything else I ran passed:

| ID | Result |
|---|---|
| G32-1 | tsc 0. Full vitest 1212/1212 (1193 + 19 new). Build ok. Biome has only the two known auth-file line-ending errors and 218 warnings. |
| G32-2 | HEAD still `1cefea1`, 9 changed files as expected, the 375 frozen hashes match, protected files 4/4. |
| G32-3 | A new anonymous browser opens the demo with no token, recording, download or R2 requests and no `Authorization` header. The token API answers 401. The paid page `/studio/middle-east` says "Sign in required", so premium access is not bypassed. A fake token gets a 500 error and no token; this is a known root item. |
| R32-DK, single steps | Each of the 5 faders ignores Delete/Backspace. Delete still works with focus on the page, on a selected clip and on the playhead. Range delete, Ctrl+Shift+L and Ctrl+Shift+X all still work. |
| R32-BC | Blur during a Pan drag while playing writes no history entry. The audio panner gets only the revert, then nothing more. A fresh drag adds 1 entry, a key step 1, pointer 42 works, and pointercancel adds nothing. The Volume reference still makes exactly 1 entry. |
| R32-K | Pan, Volume, Master, Clip Gain, Space/Home, mute/solo, fold and clip drag behave as before. |
| R32-U | Mutations aΓÇôg each made a test fail. b2 survives, which B already accepted. |
| R32-S, R32-Doc | Only the allowed hunks changed. Doc 036 matches the code. |

Two observations for B:
- **A-R32-REVIEW-1 stays open.** In the real browser the mouse pointer id is 1, and an ordinary real click clears the blocked state after a blur. While it is blocked, Pan key presses are ignored silently. Touch and pen are untested.
- **Mutation (d) named the wrong test.** It breaks two other tests, but not the "fresh drag after release" test B expected.

Not run: an optional extra mutation, because my script had a quoting error (it is not a test result), and the 1280├ù720 viewport, since this round fixed 1440├ù900.

**Ableton:** the manual says nothing about Delete on a focused fader or about pointer behaviour after focus is lost. All three of this round's behaviours are therefore unconfirmed against Ableton; they are CZABA requirements only.

Round 32's changes should not be committed until B decides on C-R32-01. Round 31's files are still ready for root's commit. All remaining carried and root items are listed in the report.
